answer: A stake-bonded registry forces every agent identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed on proven misbehavior, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand bonds. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a long verifiable history of useful work, never to fresh copies. Like pigment layered over years, trust builds slowly; like a crystal it forms one lattice at a time; at the zenith of the system only identities that survived real cost hold real weight, so an attacker pays full price for every fake.
